title: Quicklink — Shift notes & temp runbook (adhoc)
content:
Purpose: quick, thumb-rule checklist for handoff + short-term fixes that are safe to run when you’re on-call. Not a replacement for canonical runbooks (see linked Confluence), but a compressed action set for first responders.

SHIFT SUMMARY TEMPLATE (fill at end of shift)
- State: OK / DEGRADED / OUTAGE
- Key incidents during shift (1-2 line summary each with ticket id)
- What I changed (config/rollout/patch)
- What to watch first thing (metrics/alerts)
- Items to hand off (blocked PRs, ongoing mitigation)

CURRENT SHIFT BULLETPOINTS (notes while responding)
- 04:10 - model-serving autoscaler queued and flapping (see SRE-482). Short-term: scaled pool to 4 replicas, set autoscaler cooldown 90s.
- 06:34 - spike in 2xx-latency for hosted-api-us-west; traced to long prompt tail. Applied temporary request-rate limit on noisy-customer key (curl command below).
- Intermittent DB connection errors to config-store (max-conns hit). Reapplied connection-pool restart on config-service.

QUICK ACTIONS (safe, low-impact ops you can run without full approval)
- Check inference pod health: kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide | grep ready
- Restart single worker (safe): kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/inference-worker --field-manager=oncall
- Increase worker concurrency (temporary): kubectl -n inference set env deployment/inference-worker MAX_CONCURRENCY=8 && monitor 15m
- Quiet noisy API key (rate-limit): \n  curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' \n    https://api.redwood.internal/admin/keys/limit \n    -d '{"key":"<key>","rate_limit":"10r/s"}'
- Toggle fallback routing to smaller quantized model: \n  curl -X POST https://router.internal/route -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"policy":"force-quantized"}'

LOG/QUERY SNIPPETS
- Check latency tail: datadog query: avg:last_5m:percentile(inference.latency_ms{route:hosted-api},95) by {region}
- Grep recent OOM lines: kubectl -n inference logs <pod> | grep -i oom
- Recent autoscaler events: kubectl -n inference describe hpa inference-worker | sed -n '1,200p'

ESCALATION & WHO TO CALL
- Pager: on-call primary (Slack #oncall) -> if >15m unresolved, call on-call-sre (phone: internal directory)
- For infra-level hardware/GPU issues: @Ravi Patel (pager)
- For model quality regressions after rollout: @ML-ops lead (Jordan Kim)
- Exec-level incident: escalate to ops-manager + eng-ops director (see Confluence incident template)

KNOWN FLAKY THINGS / SHORT-TERM WORKAROUNDS
- Autoscaler flapping when average sequence length > 1500 tokens: workaround is to pin a lower max_batch_size on the specific model pool for the burst window (set via autoscale config).
- Token-billing spikes due to uncontrolled embeddings job: use admin key denylist to block batch job until ticket created.
- Config-store hitting max-conns: temporarly set read-only cache on app nodes (ENV:CONFIG_CACHE=true) and restart pods incrementally.

ONGOING MITIGATIONS / TODO (for next shift)
- Follow up: add autoscaler cooldown tweak to infra backlog (SRE-482).
- Create a small canary that simulates long-tail prompts to catch autoscaler flapping in CI.
- Remove temporary rate-limit on customer-abc once they replay with smaller prompts (create comms ticket).
- Add a Datadog monitor for config-store connection errors at 5 occurrences / 10m to avoid surprises.

NOTES TO SELF (scratch)
- If you restart worker, watch KV cache hit-rate — cold cache will increase latency for ~10 min.
- Avoid scaling down below 2 replicas in us-west until config-store patch rolled.
- Remember to annotate any manual change with: "oncall:maya-2025-02-02" so rollbacks are straightforward.

HANDOFF CHECKLIST (quick)
- [ ] Fill SHIFT SUMMARY TEMPLATE above (state/incidents/changes).
- [ ] Post short summary in #oncall-shift with incidents and what to watch for next 2hrs.
- [ ] Tag any tickets you created with "oncall-handled" and brief note.
- [ ] If you executed a fallback routing, file an action item in backlog to revert and verify model-level SLAs.

MISC LINKS & REFERENCES
- Canonical inference runbook: confluence://runbooks/quicklink-inference
- Datadog dashboard (latency/cost): https://datadog.redwood.ai/dashboards/inference-latency
- Incident template: confluence://incidents/incident-template

UNRESOLVED QUESTIONS
- Is there an existing playbook for temporarily throttling company-integrations (we only have customer-key blacklist so far)?
- Should we expose a safe admin toggle in the console for fallback-routing or keep it API-only? (talk to product)

END OF NOTES.
(If you're the next shift: read top of file first, then timeline; comments inline are fine — this is a living scratchpad.)
